:::{#thm-surprisal-log-half}
#### Surprisal as a logarithm to base one half

For an outcome $x$ of a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) $X$
with $\P(X=x) > 0$,
the [surprisal](#def-surprisal) in [bits](#def-bit) is

$$s(x) = \log_{1/2} \P(X=x).$$

:::

::: {.proof}

Write $p = \P(X=x)$.
The [logarithm](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm) to base $b$ equals the natural logarithm of its argument
divided by the natural logarithm of $b$
([change of base](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#rem-logarithm-formula)),
so

$$
\begin{aligned}
\log_{1/2} p
&= \frac{\logf{p}}{\logf{1/2}} \\
&= \frac{\logf{p}}{-\logf{2}} \\
&= -\frac{\logf{p}}{\logf{2}} \\
&= -\log_2 p \\
&= s(x).
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
